question.problem:
Consider the equivalence relation $∼$ on $R,$ defined by $x∼y$ if $\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi x=\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi y.$ Which of the following equivalence classes contain the element $-\frac{1}{2}?$

I. $[0]$

II. $[\frac{1}{2}]$

III. $[\frac{3}{2}]$
question.worked_solution:
We have $-\frac{1}{2}\in [x]$ if $-\frac{1}{2}∼x.$ Using the definition of the given equivalence relation, we require

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi \cdot (-\frac{1}{2})) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi x \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi x \\ -1 & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi x \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now consider each of the given equivalence classes.

- $-\frac{1}{2}\notin [0]$ because $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi \cdot 0)=0\ne -1\,\times $

- $-\frac{1}{2}\notin [\frac{1}{2}]$ because $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi \cdot \frac{1}{2})=1\ne -1\,\times $

- $-\frac{1}{2}\in [\frac{3}{2}]$ because $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi \cdot \frac{3}{2})=-1\,✓$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
